sb_prompt: DISCUSS THE CHANGES IN THE ROLES OF WOMEN IN AMERICAN SOCIETY OVER THE PAST GENERATION OR TWO.  WHICH CHANGES HAVE BEEN THE MOST SIGNIFICANT? DO YOU HAVE AN OPINION ON WHAT FURTHER CHANGES WILL TAKE PLACE OVER THE NEXT GENERATION?
turns: Yeah, exactly, that's the thing my cousin works at the courthouse and she's seen these shifts firsthand with the women she represents, it's wild how fast things moved.
Yeah, it is, but honestly I've just sort of never really seen it happen for me.
Yeah, but she says it's more than just women getting jobs, it's about how they actually carry themselves in those rooms now.
I guess I just haven't seen women in my shop really take charge of their own lives, you know?
Wait, what do you mean by that, really?
It's like they're all just trying to be liked instead of being respected, honestly.
That's harsh, but I guess what she means is that back then they just followed orders and now they're actually directing the cases.

Yeah, I guess that's the thing. I've been working here twenty years and I never really saw a woman come in and say, "Here's how I want to fix this," they just wanted me to fix whatever they brought me in to fix.
I mean, maybe it's just the kind of women who come into auto shops?
I mean, maybe I just never met the right kind of woman to ask.
Yeah, but maybe it's just the kind of women who come into auto shops?
Yeah, that's probably it, I'm in a garage after all, maybe they just don't feel safe talking like that here.
Yeah, but I think you're overlooking the fact that more women are actually owning the shops now, not just working in them.
That's a fair point, but I still haven't seen that ownership translate to the women actually calling the shots in the shop.
Oh really? That's kind of crazy, I have a cousin who actually owns her own firm now and she tells me she makes all the decisions herself.
Yeah, but she's got a husband who runs the books and handles the client calls, so she's basically just managing the schedule and making coffee.
Wait, really? She lets you handle the client calls?
Yeah, honestly, she basically just does the paperwork and I deal with the clients, which is weird for a woman to have that role but here we are.
That's... that's pretty wild for a wife and husband to split it up like that, isn't it?
Yeah, it is, I mean, it's just not how I picture a woman leading a business.
That sounds like the opposite of leadership to me, isn't it?

Yeah, but then again, maybe he's doing it because she's the boss and he knows she won't fire him if she handles the schedule, whereas if a woman just came in and took over the client calls, people would just assume she doesn't know what she's talking about.
That actually makes total sense, because let's face it, if I told a customer I was the boss and then made a mechanical diagnosis, half the guys in my line would just laugh right in your face.
Yeah, I guess you're right, but it still feels like they're just checking boxes and not actually doing the heavy lifting.
That's true, but at least I know my cousin has the final say on when we take time off and what we charge.
Yeah, but even then, I still feel like she's just playing the office manager role while the real power stays with the old guys from the original partnership.
I guess she's just protecting her spot by keeping the clients away from her, but honestly that feels like settling for less than she deserves.
Yeah, but even if she gets the title, does anyone really listen to her anymore?
I guess if she doesn't let anyone else touch the money, at least the power isn't just sitting there on a shelf anymore.
Yeah, but if she can't even get the guys to listen to her diagnosis, what good is having the final say really?
Well, at least she gets the final say on the money, which is the only thing that really counts in the end.
Yeah, but if the guys don't trust her judgment on the repairs, can she really stop them from fixing it wrong even when she says no?
I mean, if the money stays in her hands, she can just refuse to pay for the bad parts and force them to listen.
Well, if the guys know she's got the cash, they might actually start listening to her, but it takes a long time for that kind of respect to stick once people get used to the old way.
Yeah, if she controls the wallet they have to pay, they'll probably listen even if they don't trust her car knowledge yet.
Yeah, but once she finally gets them to listen to her diagnosis, will she actually have the guts to tell a customer to fix it somewhere else if they want to?
Yeah, but if she's paying for it she has to be right, right?
Yeah, but if she tells a customer to go somewhere else, the guys will just say she's cheap and pass the bill back to him anyway.
But if she's the one writing the check, she's got the power to just walk out of there if they try to push her.
Yeah, but if she can't make them listen without the customers fighting her, is she really the boss?
